newsitem.title: CHINA: China capital exports up 3.6 pct in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: China capital exports up 3.6 pct in first quarter.

text.p: Exports by China's capital, Beijing, rose slightly in the first three months, up by 3.6 percent compared with the year-ago period, the Xinhua news agency said.
The capital's foreign trade maintained steady growth, with foreign trade totalling $704 million. Of that exports accounted for $470 million and imports $234 million, it said in an overnight report.
The increase in exports after a drop in the same period last year came mainly from trade by foreign joint ventures, it said.
In January-March, exports by joint ventures reached $180 million, soaring 51.3 percent from the same period last year, and accounting for 38.4 percent of the city's total.
Machinery and electronic products were the major export items of joint ventures, it said.
The processing trade also reported an increase to account for 55.9 percent of the total, it said.
The city planned to export $2.3 billion worth of goods in 1997, it said.
